sanskrit: sa bhavān astu naḥ śūraḥ praṇetā vāhinīmukhe raṇaṃ ca yāte bhavati pāṇḍavā mandacetasaḥ bhaviṣyanti sahāmātyāḥ pāñcālāś ca nirudyamāḥ
english: Be you then our hero, our leader at the head of the host; and when you have entered the battle, the Pāṇḍavas will grow faint of heart, and the Pāñcālas too, with their counsellors, will be robbed of their resolve.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca yat tu māṃ manyase rājan kururāja karomi tat tvatpriyārthaṃ hi me sarvaṃ prāṇā rājyaṃ dhanāni ca
english: Śalya said: Whatever you would have of me, O king of the Kurus, that I will do; for your pleasure all that is mine — my life, my kingdom, my wealth — is yours.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca senāpatyena varaye tvām ahaṃ mātulātulam so 'smān pāhi yudhāṃ śreṣṭha skando devān ivāhave
english: Duryodhana said: I choose you, my peerless uncle, for the command of the army. Guard us, O best of warriors, as Skanda guards the gods in battle.

sanskrit: abhiṣicyasva rājendra devānām iva pāvakiḥ jahi śatrūn raṇe vīra mahendro dānavān iva
english: Be consecrated, O lord of kings, as the son of Fire was consecrated by the gods; slay the foes in battle, O hero, as great Indra slew the Dānavas.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca etac chrutvā vaco rājño madrarājaḥ pratāpavān duryodhanaṃ tadā rājan vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Saṃjaya said: Having heard these words of the king, the mighty lord of the Madras then, O king, spoke this speech to Duryodhana.

sanskrit: duryodhana mahābāho śṛṇu vākyavidāṃ vara yāv etau manyase kṛṣṇau rathasthau rathināṃ varau na me tulyāv ubhāv etau bāhuvīrye kathaṃ cana
english: O mighty-armed Duryodhana, hear, best of those skilled in speech: these two Kṛṣṇas whom you reckon, the foremost of chariot-warriors mounted on their car — neither of them is in any way my equal in the prowess of arm.

sanskrit: udyatāṃ pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ sasurāsuramānavām yodhayeyaṃ raṇamukhe saṃkruddhaḥ kim u pāṇḍavān vijeṣye ca raṇe pārthān somakāṃś ca samāgatān
english: Roused to wrath, I would do battle at the front of the fray with the whole earth in arms, with its gods and Asuras and men — how much more the Pāṇḍavas! I shall conquer in the field the sons of Pṛthā and the Somakas gathered together.

sanskrit: ahaṃ senāpraṇetā te bhaviṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ taṃ ca vyūhaṃ vidhāsyāmi na tariṣyanti yaṃ pare iti satyaṃ bravīmy eṣa duryodhana na saṃśayaḥ
english: I will be the leader of your army, of that there is no doubt; and I will array such a battle-formation as the enemy shall not cross. This I tell you truly, Duryodhana, beyond all doubt.

sanskrit: evam uktas tato rājā madrādhipatim añjasā abhyaṣiñcata senāyā madhye bharatasattama vidhinā śāstradṛṣṭena hṛṣṭarūpo viśāṃ pate
english: Thus addressed, the king straightway consecrated the lord of the Madras in the midst of the army, O best of the Bharatas, by the rite ordained in scripture, his countenance full of joy, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: abhiṣikte tatas tasmin siṃhanādo mahān abhūt tava sainyeṣv avādyanta vāditrāṇi ca bhārata
english: When he had been consecrated, a great lion-roar arose throughout your forces, O Bhārata, and the instruments of music were sounded.

sanskrit: hṛṣṭāś cāsaṃs tadā yodhā madrakāś ca mahārathāḥ tuṣṭuvuś caiva rājānaṃ śalyam āhavaśobhinam
english: The warriors then were filled with gladness, and the mighty car-warriors of the Madras, and they praised king Śalya, the splendour of the battlefield.

sanskrit: jaya rājaṃś ciraṃ jīva jahi śatrūn samāgatān tava bāhubalaṃ prāpya dhārtarāṣṭrā mahābalāḥ nikhilāṃ pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ praśāsantu hatadviṣaḥ
english: Conquer, O king! Live long! Slay the foes assembled! Having gained the strength of your arms, may the mighty sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, their enemies slain, rule over the whole of this entire earth.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi śakto raṇe jetuṃ sasurāsuramānavān martyadharmāṇa iha tu kim u somakasṛñjayān
english: For you are able to vanquish in battle the gods, Asuras, and men together; how much more these Somakas and Sṛñjayas, who are but mortal in their nature.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃstūyamānas tu madrāṇām adhipo balī harṣaṃ prāpa tadā vīro durāpam akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: Thus extolled, the mighty lord of the Madras, that hero, felt then a joy hard for the unrestrained of soul to attain.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca adyaivāhaṃ raṇe sarvān pāñcālān saha pāṇḍavaiḥ nihaniṣyāmi rājendra svargaṃ yāsyāmi vā hataḥ
english: Śalya said: This very day, O lord of kings, I shall slay in battle all the Pāñcālas together with the Pāṇḍavas, or, slain myself, shall go to heaven.

sanskrit: adya paśyantu māṃ lokā vicarantam abhītavat adya pāṇḍusutāḥ sarve vāsudevaḥ sasātyakiḥ
english: This day let all the worlds behold me roaming fearless; this day let all the sons of Pāṇḍu, and Vāsudeva with Sātyaki,

sanskrit: pāñcālāś cedayaś caiva draupadeyāś ca sarvaśaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca sarve cāpi prabhadrakāḥ
english: the Pāñcālas and the Cedis, and the sons of Draupadī one and all, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin and all the Prabhadrakas as well —

sanskrit: vikramaṃ mama paśyantu dhanuṣaś ca mahad balam lāghavaṃ cāstravīryaṃ ca bhujayoś ca balaṃ yudhi
english: let them behold my valour, the great power of my bow, my swiftness of hand, the force of my weapons, and the strength of my arms in the fray.

sanskrit: adya paśyantu me pārthāḥ siddhāś ca saha cāraṇaiḥ yādṛśaṃ me balaṃ bāhvoḥ saṃpad astreṣu yā ca me
english: This day let the sons of Pṛthā behold, and the Siddhas with the Cāraṇas, what is the strength of my arms and what mastery is mine in weapons.

sanskrit: adya me vikramaṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ pratīkāraparā bhūtvā ceṣṭantāṃ vividhāḥ kriyāḥ
english: This day, beholding my valour, let the mighty car-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, bent on resistance, attempt their manifold counter-measures.

sanskrit: adya sainyāni pāṇḍūnāṃ drāvayiṣye samantataḥ droṇabhīṣmāv ati vibho sūtaputraṃ ca saṃyuge vicariṣye raṇe yudhyan priyārthaṃ tava kaurava
english: This day I shall scatter the armies of the Pāṇḍus on every side, O lord, surpassing Droṇa and Bhīṣma and the son of the charioteer in the encounter; fighting in battle I shall range about for your pleasure, O Kaurava.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca abhiṣikte tadā śalye tava sainyeṣu mānada na karṇavyasanaṃ kiṃ cin menire tatra bhārata
english: Saṃjaya said: When Śalya had thus been consecrated, O giver of honour, your forces no longer reckoned the loss of Karṇa as any calamity at all, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: hṛṣṭāḥ sumanasaś caiva babhūvus tatra sainikāḥ menire nihatān pārthān madrarājavaśaṃ gatān
english: Glad and good of heart the soldiers there became; they reckoned the sons of Pṛthā as already slain, fallen into the power of the king of the Madras.

sanskrit: praharṣaṃ prāpya senā tu tāvakī bharatarṣabha tāṃ rātriṃ sukhinī suptā svasthacitteva sābhavat
english: Having gained delight, your army, O bull of the Bharatas, slept happily through that night, and became as one whose mind was at ease.

sanskrit: sainyasya tava taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vārṣṇeyam abravīd vākyaṃ sarvakṣatrasya śṛṇvataḥ
english: Hearing that clamour of your host, king Yudhiṣṭhira spoke these words to the scion of the Vṛṣṇis, within hearing of all the warrior-kind.

sanskrit: madrarājaḥ kṛtaḥ śalyo dhārtarāṣṭreṇa mādhava senāpatir maheṣvāsaḥ sarvasainyeṣu pūjitaḥ
english: Śalya, king of the Madras, has been made commander by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Mādhava — that mighty archer, honoured throughout all the forces.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā yathābhūtaṃ kuru mādhava yat kṣamam bhavān netā ca goptā ca vidhatsva yad anantaram
english: Having heard this as it truly is, do, O Mādhava, what is fitting. You are our guide and our protector; ordain what should next be done.

sanskrit: tam abravīn mahārāja vāsudevo janādhipam ārtāyanim ahaṃ jāne yathātattvena bhārata
english: To him, O great king, spoke Vāsudeva, the lord of men: I know the son of Ṛtāyana truly as he is, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vīryavāṃś ca mahātejā mahātmā ca viśeṣataḥ kṛtī ca citrayodhī ca saṃyukto lāghavena ca
english: He is valiant and of great splendour, and high-souled above the rest; accomplished and varied in the modes of combat, and endowed with swiftness of hand.

sanskrit: yādṛg bhīṣmas tathā droṇo yādṛk karṇaś ca saṃyuge tādṛśas tad viśiṣṭo vā madrarājo mato mama
english: Such as Bhīṣma was, and Droṇa, and such as Karṇa was in the encounter — such, or even greater, do I deem the king of the Madras to be.

sanskrit: yudhyamānasya tasyājau cintayann eva bhārata yoddhāraṃ nādhigacchāmi tulyarūpaṃ janādhipa
english: Pondering on him as he fights in the field, O Bhārata, I can find no warrior of equal stature to oppose him, O lord of men.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍyarjunabhīmānāṃ sātvatasya ca bhārata dhṛṣṭadyumnasya ca tathā balenābhyadhiko raṇe
english: In strength he surpasses, in battle, Śikhaṇḍin, Arjuna, and Bhīma, and the Sātvata too, O Bhārata, and likewise Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: madrarājo mahārāja siṃhadviradavikramaḥ vicariṣyaty abhīḥ kāle kālaḥ kruddhaḥ prajāsv iva
english: The king of the Madras, O great king, with the prowess of a lion and an elephant, will range about fearless when the hour comes, like wrathful Death among living creatures.

sanskrit: tasyādya na prapaśyāmi pratiyoddhāram āhave tvām ṛte puruṣavyāghra śārdūlasamavikramam
english: For him this day I see no fit antagonist in battle save you, O tiger among men, you whose valour is like a tiger's.

sanskrit: sadevaloke kṛtsne 'smin nānyas tvattaḥ pumān bhavet madrarājaṃ raṇe kruddhaṃ yo hanyāt kurunandana ahany ahani yudhyantaṃ kṣobhayantaṃ balaṃ tava
english: In all this world of the gods there is no man but you, O joy of the Kurus, who could slay in battle the king of the Madras when roused — him who, fighting day after day, throws your host into turmoil.

sanskrit: tasmāj jahi raṇe śalyaṃ maghavān iva śambaram atipaścād asau vīro dhārtarāṣṭreṇa satkṛtaḥ
english: Therefore slay Śalya in battle as Maghavat slew Śambara. That hero has, at this last, been honoured by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tavaiva hi jayo nūnaṃ hate madreśvare yudhi tasmin hate hataṃ sarvaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrabalaṃ mahat
english: Surely the victory is yours alone, once the lord of the Madras is slain in the fight; when he is slain, the whole great host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son is slain.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā mahārāja vacanaṃ mama sāṃpratam pratyudyāhi raṇe pārtha madrarājaṃ mahābalam jahi cainaṃ mahābāho vāsavo namuciṃ yathā
english: Having heard, O great king, this my timely counsel, go forth in battle, O son of Pṛthā, against the mighty king of the Madras, and slay him, O mighty-armed one, as Vāsava slew Namuci.

sanskrit: na caivātra dayā kāryā mātulo 'yaṃ mameti vai kṣatradharmaṃ puraskṛtya jahi madrajaneśvaram
english: And here let no pity be shown, with the thought 'this is my uncle'; setting the law of the warrior foremost, slay the lord of the Madra folk.

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇārṇavaṃ tīrtvā karṇapātālasaṃbhavam mā nimajjasva sagaṇaḥ śalyam āsādya goṣpadam
english: Having crossed the ocean of Bhīṣma and Droṇa, with the abyss that was Karṇa, do not, with your followers, sink in coming upon Śalya, who is but a puddle in a cow's hoof-print.

sanskrit: yac ca te tapaso vīryaṃ yac ca kṣātraṃ balaṃ tava tad darśaya raṇe sarvaṃ jahi cainaṃ mahāratham
english: Whatever is the power of your austerity, and whatever your warrior strength, show it all forth in the battle, and slay that mighty car-warrior.

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ keśavaḥ paravīrahā jagāma śibiraṃ sāyaṃ pūjyamāno 'tha pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: Having spoken these words, Keśava, the slayer of hostile heroes, went at evening to his camp, honoured then by the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: keśave tu tadā yāte dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ visṛjya sarvān bhrātṝṃś ca pāñcālān atha somakān suṣvāpa rajanīṃ tāṃ tu viśalya iva kuñjaraḥ
english: When Keśava had departed, Yudhiṣṭhira the king of righteousness dismissed all his brothers and the Pāñcālas and the Somakas, and slept through that night like an elephant from whom the dart has been drawn.

sanskrit: te ca sarve maheṣvāsāḥ pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavās tathā karṇasya nidhane hṛṣṭāḥ suṣupus tāṃ niśāṃ tadā
english: And all those mighty archers, the Pāñcālas and the Pāṇḍavas alike, rejoicing in the death of Karṇa, slept through that night.

sanskrit: gatajvaraṃ maheṣvāsaṃ tīrṇapāraṃ mahāratham babhūva pāṇḍaveyānāṃ sainyaṃ pramuditaṃ niśi sūtaputrasya nidhane jayaṃ labdhvā ca māriṣa
english: Its fever gone, having reached the farther shore — that host of the Pāṇḍavas, of mighty archers and great car-warriors, was filled with delight in the night, having won victory in the slaying of the charioteer's son, O sire.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vyatītāyāṃ rajanyāṃ tu rājā duryodhanas tadā abravīt tāvakān sarvān saṃnahyantāṃ mahārathāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When the night had passed, king Duryodhana then said to all your men: Let the mighty car-warriors arm themselves.

sanskrit: rājñas tu matam ājñāya samanahyata sā camūḥ ayojayan rathāṃs tūrṇaṃ paryadhāvaṃs tathāpare
english: Knowing the king's intent, that army armed itself; some yoked the chariots in haste, while others ran about on every side.

sanskrit: akalpyanta ca mātaṅgāḥ samanahyanta pattayaḥ hayān āstaraṇopetāṃś cakrur anye sahasraśaḥ
english: The elephants were caparisoned, the foot-soldiers donned their armour, and others by the thousand made ready the horses with their housings.

sanskrit: vāditrāṇāṃ ca ninadaḥ prādurāsīd viśāṃ pate bodhanārthaṃ hi yodhānāṃ sainyānāṃ cāpy udīryatām
english: The din of musical instruments arose, O lord of peoples, to rouse the warriors and to stir up the troops as they marshalled.

sanskrit: tato balāni sarvāṇi senāśiṣṭāni bhārata saṃnaddhāny eva dadṛśur mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam
english: Then all the forces, what remained of the army, O Bhārata, fully armed, were seen having made death their place of return.

sanskrit: śalyaṃ senāpatiṃ kṛtvā madrarājaṃ mahārathāḥ pravibhajya balaṃ sarvam anīkeṣu vyavasthitāḥ
english: Having made Śalya, king of the Madras, their commander, the great car-warriors apportioned the whole host and took their stations in the divisions.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve samāgamya putreṇa tava sainikāḥ kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca drauṇiḥ śalyo 'tha saubalaḥ
english: Then all the warriors, gathering together with your son — Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman, the son of Droṇa, Śalya, and the son of Subala —

sanskrit: anye ca pārthivāḥ śeṣāḥ samayaṃ cakrire tadā na na ekena yoddhavyaṃ kathaṃ cid api pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: and the other kings who remained, then made this compact: that not one of them should ever fight singly against the Pāṇḍavas in any way.

sanskrit: yo hy ekaḥ pāṇḍavair yudhyed yo vā yudhyantam utsṛjet sa pañcabhir bhaved yuktaḥ pātakaiḥ sopapātakaiḥ anyonyaṃ parirakṣadbhir yoddhavyaṃ sahitaiś ca naḥ
english: For whoever should fight singly against the Pāṇḍavas, or should abandon a comrade who was fighting, he would be joined to the five great sins together with the lesser sins; we must fight together, guarding one another.

sanskrit: evaṃ te samayaṃ kṛtvā sarve tatra mahārathāḥ madrarājaṃ puraskṛtya tūrṇam abhyadravan parān
english: Having thus made their compact, all those great car-warriors there, placing the king of the Madras at their head, swiftly rushed against the foe.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavā rājan vyūhya sainyaṃ mahāraṇe abhyayuḥ kauravān sarvān yotsyamānāḥ samantataḥ
english: Even so the Pāṇḍavas, O king, having arrayed their host for the great battle, advanced against all the Kauravas, ready to do combat on every side.

sanskrit: tad balaṃ bharataśreṣṭha kṣubdhārṇavasamasvanam samuddhūtārṇavākāram uddhūtarathakuñjaram
english: That host, O best of the Bharatas, roared like a tossing sea; with its uplifted chariots and elephants it had the very semblance of a heaving ocean.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca droṇasya bhīṣmasya ca vai rādheyasya ca me śrutam pātanaṃ śaṃsa me bhūyaḥ śalyasyātha sutasya me
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Of the fall of Droṇa and of Bhīṣma and of the son of Rādhā I have heard; tell me now further of the fall of Śalya, and of my son.

sanskrit: kathaṃ raṇe hataḥ śalyo dharmarājena saṃjaya bhīmena ca mahābāhuḥ putro duryodhano mama
english: How was Śalya slain in battle by the king of righteousness, O Saṃjaya? And how was my mighty-armed son Duryodhana slain by Bhīma?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca kṣayaṃ manuṣyadehānāṃ rathanāgāśvasaṃkṣayam śṛṇu rājan sthiro bhūtvā saṃgrāmaṃ śaṃsato mama
english: Saṃjaya said: The destruction of human bodies, the ruin of chariots, elephants, and horses — hear it, O king, with steady mind, as I recount the battle.

sanskrit: āśā balavatī rājan putrāṇāṃ te 'bhavat tadā hate bhīṣme ca droṇe ca sūtaputre ca pātite śalyaḥ pārthān raṇe sarvān nihaniṣyati māriṣa
english: A strong hope then arose, O king, in your sons, even when Bhīṣma was slain and Droṇa and the charioteer's son struck down: that Śalya would slay all the sons of Pṛthā in battle, O sire.

sanskrit: tām āśāṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā samāśvāsya ca bhārata madrarājaṃ ca samare samāśritya mahāratham nāthavantam athātmānam amanyata sutas tava
english: Holding that hope in his heart, and taking comfort, O Bhārata, and leaning in the fray upon the king of the Madras, that great car-warrior, your son deemed himself to have a protector.

sanskrit: yadā karṇe hate pārthāḥ siṃhanādaṃ pracakrire tadā rājan dhārtarāṣṭrān āviveśa mahad bhayam
english: When, Karṇa being slain, the sons of Pṛthā raised their lion-roar, then, O king, a great fear entered the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tān samāśvāsya tu tadā madrarājaḥ pratāpavān vyūhya vyūhaṃ mahārāja sarvatobhadram ṛddhimat
english: But the valiant king of the Madras, having reassured them, then arrayed, O great king, the prosperous Sarvatobhadra formation.

sanskrit: pratyudyāto raṇe pārthān madrarājaḥ pratāpavān vidhunvan kārmukaṃ citraṃ bhāraghnaṃ vegavattaram
english: The valiant king of the Madras went forth in battle against the sons of Pṛthā, brandishing his bright bow, crushing of burdens and exceedingly swift.

sanskrit: rathapravaram āsthāya saindhavāśvaṃ mahārathaḥ tasya sītā mahārāja rathasthāśobhayad ratham
english: That great car-warrior, mounting his foremost chariot drawn by horses of the Sindhu, had its banner-pole, O great king, set upon the car, adorning it.

sanskrit: sa tena saṃvṛto vīro rathenāmitrakarśanaḥ tasthau śūro mahārāja putrāṇāṃ te bhayapraṇut
english: Encompassed by that chariot, the hero, scourge of foes, stood firm, O great king — that warrior who dispelled the fear of your sons.

sanskrit: prayāṇe madrarājo 'bhūn mukhaṃ vyūhasya daṃśitaḥ madrakaiḥ sahito vīraiḥ karṇaputraiś ca durjayaiḥ
english: On the march the king of the Madras, armoured, formed the front of the formation, together with the heroic Madrakas and the invincible sons of Karṇa.

sanskrit: savye 'bhūt kṛtavarmā ca trigartaiḥ parivāritaḥ gautamo dakṣiṇe pārśve śakaiś ca yavanaiḥ saha
english: On the left was Kṛtavarman, surrounded by the Trigartas; the son of Gautama held the right flank, with the Śakas and the Yavanas.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā pṛṣṭhato 'bhūt kāmbojaiḥ parivāritaḥ duryodhano 'bhavan madhye rakṣitaḥ kurupuṃgavaiḥ
english: Aśvatthāman was at the rear, surrounded by the Kāmbojas; Duryodhana was in the centre, guarded by the bulls of the Kurus.

sanskrit: hayānīkena mahatā saubalaś cāpi saṃvṛtaḥ prayayau sarvasainyena kaitavyaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: With a great body of horse the son of Subala too, surrounded, marched forth with all his troops, and the prince of the Kaitavyas, that great car-warrior.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś ca maheṣvāsā vyūhya sainyam ariṃdamāḥ tridhā bhūtvā mahārāja tava sainyam upādravan
english: And the Pāṇḍavas, those mighty archers and tamers of foes, having arrayed their host and divided it into three, O great king, fell upon your army.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ śalyasya vāhinīṃ tūrṇam abhidudruvur āhave
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin and Sātyaki, that great car-warrior, swiftly charged against the host of Śalya in the battle.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā svenānīkena saṃvṛtaḥ śalyam evābhidudrāva jighāṃsur bharatarṣabha
english: Then king Yudhiṣṭhira, surrounded by his own division, charged straight at Śalya, seeking to slay him, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: hārdikyaṃ tu maheṣvāsam arjunaḥ śatrupūgahā saṃśaptakagaṇāṃś caiva vegato 'bhividudruve
english: But Arjuna, slayer of hosts of foes, swiftly charged against Hārdikya, that mighty archer, and against the bands of the Saṃśaptakas.

sanskrit: gautamaṃ bhīmaseno vai somakāś ca mahārathāḥ abhyadravanta rājendra jighāṃsantaḥ parān yudhi
english: Bhīmasena and the Somaka great car-warriors charged against the son of Gautama, O lord of kings, seeking to slay the foe in the fight.

sanskrit: mādrīputrau tu śakunim ulūkaṃ ca mahārathau sasainyau sahasenau tāv upatasthatur āhave
english: And the two sons of Mādrī, those great car-warriors, with their troops and forces, stood up in battle against Śakuni and Ulūka.

sanskrit: tathaivāyutaśo yodhās tāvakāḥ pāṇḍavān raṇe abhyadravanta saṃkruddhā vividhāyudhapāṇayaḥ
english: Even so your warriors by tens of thousands rushed against the Pāṇḍavas in the battle, full of wrath, with manifold weapons in their hands.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca hate bhīṣme maheṣvāse droṇe karṇe mahārathe kuruṣv alpāvaśiṣṭeṣu pāṇḍaveṣu ca saṃyuge
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When Bhīṣma the mighty archer was slain, and Droṇa, and Karṇa the great car-warrior, when the Kurus were left but few, and the Pāṇḍavas too, in the war —

sanskrit: susaṃrabdheṣu pārtheṣu parākrānteṣu saṃjaya māmakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca kiṃ śiṣṭam abhavad balam
english: when the sons of Pṛthā were sorely roused and pressing on, O Saṃjaya, what strength remained, of mine and of the foe?
